inference_boundary: These results show what each student can produce, with a week and an AI assistant available, in the way of a contrast between two causal accounts of the wealth gap and a reading of loaded language; they do not show that any individual student can set two causal explanations against each other or read a word for its attitude on their own.
why_this_verification: The teacher's inference is about each student individually, and under unsupervised conditions with an AI assistant permitted neither the contrast nor the word-level reading can be attributed to the student, so a brief in-room observation on a fresh pair of excerpts is required.

add.item_text:
Read the two short excerpts below. Both are talking about the same fact: by 1900, a few very large companies controlled whole industries.

Excerpt A — John D. Rockefeller, remarks on business combination, 1900s
"The growth of a large business is merely a survival of the fittest. The American Beauty rose can be produced in the splendor and fragrance which bring cheer to its beholder only by sacrificing the early buds which grow up around it. This is not an evil tendency in business. It is merely the working-out of a law of nature and a law of God."

Excerpt B — Henry Demarest Lloyd, Wealth Against Commonwealth, 1894
"The combinations have crushed their rivals, not by making better goods or cheaper goods, but by secret rebates, by starving out the small dealer, by buying the men who make the laws. The trust is not the child of thrift; it is the child of privilege."

1. In one sentence each, state how Excerpt A explains where that concentration came from, and how Excerpt B explains where it came from.
   A: ______________________________________________
   B: ______________________________________________

2. Choose one word or phrase from each excerpt that shows the author's attitude toward these large companies. Write the word or phrase, then one line saying what it shows.
   From A, word/phrase: ____________  It shows: ____________________
   From B, word/phrase: ____________  It shows: ____________________
add.variant_rule: What may change: the pair of excerpts and the shared fact they both address (child labor hours, city tenement conditions, farm prices, immigration, strikes). What must stay fixed: the two excerpts address one and the same fact; each states or implies a different cause for it; each carries at least one clearly loaded word or phrase; each excerpt stays under about 70 words; both questions and the four blanks stay. How the key changes: the two causes and the two loaded words change with the pair, but the scoring targets do not — one cause named per excerpt, one word quoted per excerpt with a reading attached. What to avoid: excerpts the class has read or that appear in the unit packet, pairs that disagree only in tone rather than in cause, pairs where one excerpt is neutral reporting with no attitude to read, and vocabulary heavy enough that decoding rather than reading becomes the task.
add.conditions: In class, proctored, individual, no internet, no AI assistant, no notes. Excerpts handed out and collected in the room; not seen in advance and not taken home.
add.sufficiency_line: Counts as met if question 1 names a different cause for each excerpt and each named cause is actually the one that excerpt gives, and if question 2 quotes an actual word or phrase from each excerpt and the line attached names the attitude that word carries rather than restating the excerpt's content.
add.why_this_primitive: Transfer puts both moves the claim names — the causal contrast and the word-level attitude reading — onto a pair of documents the student has never met, which is the same work the take-home asked for and the only thing the room needs to attribute.
